request.spec:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added patrons and backing. All 4 Playwright tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**How it works**
- **Adding a patron:** each person's row has a list of people on the sheet (`person-patron-select`) and an Add button (`person-patron-add`). Picking yourself, or someone who is already your patron, is refused. The refusal shows `person-patron-error` on the row and writes nothing to the store or the audit file. The server makes the same checks, so a page that is out of date can't get around them.
- **Audit:** a successful add writes `PATRON_ADDED sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> patron=<patron name>`.
- **Showing patrons:** `person-patrons` lists the patrons' current names, sorted and joined with ", ". Patrons are stored by id, so renaming a person updates every list they appear in.
- **Backing:** `person-backing` adds up the patrons' due-totals, skipping any shown as n/a, and shows 0.00 when there are no patrons. It is worked out in the browser the same way as the existing due-total, so holding a patron changes it straight away; for example, holding Ben drops Ada's backing from 2.00 to 0.00.

**Where the changes are**
- **Stored data:** a new table, `person_patron`, in migration `V22__person_patron.sql`, keyed on the person and the patron, with a check that the two differ.
- **Server:**
  - `Person` holds its patron ids.
  - A new `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/patrons` endpoint (body `{ patronId }`) goes through `PersonService.addPatron`.
  - The person data the server returns now includes `patronIds`.
- **Front end:** the new methods are in `core/people.ts`, and the new columns and controls in `features/people/people.ts`.

**Choices you might want to revisit**
- The list offers every person on the sheet, including the person themselves and retired people, and the server refuses the invalid picks. A retired patron still counts toward backing.
- Adding a patron counts as saving the person, so the person's version goes up. If someone else has that person open in the edit form, their save will be refused with the usual "someone else has saved this person" message.
